title: Linear arithmetic with omega
summary: Close linear integer and natural-number inequalities in one step using omega.
code: theorem nat_sandwich (a b : Nat) (h1 : a <= b) (h2 : b <= a) : a = b := by
triggers: prove an equality or inequality over Nat or Int from linear hypotheses
discharge arithmetic side conditions after splitting cases
prompts: You have a <= b and b <= a on natural numbers and need to conclude a = b.
Two linear bounds on Nat indices imply equality without manual Nat.le_antisymm.
invariant: omega decides quantifier-free Presburger arithmetic over Nat and Int.
mantra: Linear Nat or Int bounds in context? Reach for omega first.
pitfalls: omega does not unfold custom definitions unless you have already dsimp or simp them.
Non-linear multiplication between variables requires nlinarith or ring, not omega.

anchors.name: Presburger decision
anchors.trick: Let omega combine linear inequalities and antisymmetry automatically.

mutations.explanation: rfl only closes definitional equalities, not propositional antisymmetry.
